findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or repository access can read them and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables holding secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed Lambda key, which any principal able to describe the function can implicitly use to view the values in plaintext. A customer-managed CMK would add key-policy-based access control over the secrets at rest.
The function uses nodejs12.x, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime unpatched.

No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so the deployment package is not verified against a trusted signing profile; an attacker able to write to the deployment artifact or invoke UpdateFunctionCode can substitute malicious code that will execute with the function's IAM role.
